title: SQL Set 07: SaaS Subscriptions, Cohorts & Telemetry
description: Active subscription overlap checks, consecutive login streaks, plan upgrade detection, and percentile/median style queries.

queries.title: Users Who Upgraded from Free to Paid Plan
queries.prompt: Find `user_id` of users whose `plan` transitioned directly from `'FREE'` to `'PRO'` or `'ENTERPRISE'` on their immediately next event ordered by `changed_at`. Order by `user_id`.
queries.schemaSql: CREATE TABLE plan_history (ev_id INT PRIMARY KEY, user_id INT, changed_at TEXT, plan TEXT);
queries.solutionSql: WITH nxt AS (SELECT user_id, plan, LEAD(plan) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY changed_at, ev_id) AS next_plan FROM plan_history) SELECT DISTINCT user_id FROM nxt WHERE plan = 'FREE' AND next_plan IN ('PRO', 'ENTERPRISE') ORDER BY user_id;
queries.explanation: `LEAD(plan)` inspects the immediately following subscription event per user without expensive self-joins.

queries.title: Monthly Recurring Revenue by Active Tier
queries.prompt: Join `subscriptions` and `plans` to calculate `tier_name` and `active_mrr` (`SUM(monthly_price)`) for rows where `status = 'ACTIVE'`. Include tiers with 0 active subscriptions (`0` MRR). Order by `active_mrr` descending, `tier_name` ascending.
queries.schemaSql: CREATE TABLE plans (tier_id INT PRIMARY KEY, tier_name TEXT, monthly_price INT); CREATE TABLE subscriptions (sub_id INT PRIMARY KEY, tier_id INT, status TEXT);
queries.seedSql: INSERT INTO plans VALUES (1,'Starter',500),(2,'Growth',1500),(3,'Scale',4000); INSERT INTO subscriptions VALUES (10,1,'ACTIVE'),(11,1,'CANCELLED'),(12,2,'ACTIVE'),(13,2,'ACTIVE');
queries.solutionSql: SELECT p.tier_name, COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN s.status = 'ACTIVE' THEN p.monthly_price ELSE 0 END), 0) AS active_mrr FROM plans p LEFT JOIN subscriptions s ON p.tier_id = s.tier_id GROUP BY p.tier_id, p.tier_name ORDER BY active_mrr DESC, p.tier_name ASC;
queries.explanation: Putting `s.status = 'ACTIVE'` in `CASE` (or in the `LEFT JOIN ... ON` clause rather than `WHERE`) preserves the zero-active `Scale` tier.

queries.title: Users with 3+ Consecutive Daily Logins
queries.prompt: Given `user_logins (user_id, login_date)` (already deduplicated per day), find `user_id` values who logged in on at least 3 consecutive calendar days. Order by `user_id`.
queries.schemaSql: CREATE TABLE user_logins (user_id INT, login_date TEXT);
queries.solutionSql: WITH grp AS (SELECT user_id, julianday(login_date) - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY login_date) AS island FROM user_logins) SELECT DISTINCT user_id FROM grp GROUP BY user_id, island HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3 ORDER BY user_id;
queries.explanation: Subtracting `ROW_NUMBER()` from `julianday(login_date)` stays constant across consecutive calendar days (classic Gaps & Islands pattern).

queries.title: Endpoints with P95-Style Max Latency > 2x Average
queries.prompt: For each `endpoint` in `api_logs`, return `endpoint` and `max_ms` where `MAX(latency_ms) > 2 * AVG(latency_ms)` and at least 3 requests were logged. Order by `endpoint`.
queries.schemaSql: CREATE TABLE api_logs (req_id INT PRIMARY KEY, endpoint TEXT, latency_ms INT);
queries.solutionSql: SELECT endpoint, MAX(latency_ms) AS max_ms FROM api_logs GROUP BY endpoint HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3 AND MAX(latency_ms) > 2 * AVG(latency_ms) ORDER BY endpoint;
queries.explanation: `/search` has avg 300 and max 900 (> 600); `/health` only has 2 requests.

queries.title: Browser Traffic Share Percentage
queries.prompt: Calculate `browser` and `share_pct` (`ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (), 2)`) from `sessions`. Order by `share_pct` DESC, `browser` ASC.
queries.schemaSql: CREATE TABLE sessions (sess_id INT PRIMARY KEY, browser TEXT);
queries.solutionSql: SELECT browser, ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (), 2) AS share_pct FROM sessions GROUP BY browser ORDER BY share_pct DESC, browser ASC;
queries.explanation: `SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER ()` sums the grouped counts across the entire result set without needing a separate CTE.
